reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates a 3× TBReff reduction via nanoscale trenches at a GaN/diamond interface, supporting the premise that nanopatterning can reduce thermal boundary resistance. However, the evidence is from a completely different material system (semiconductor-on-diamond) and does not address refractory HEAs, plasma-facing conditions, mechanical integrity, or pattern durability under the proposed extreme environment. The key premises regarding HEA applicability, structural integrity, and high-temperature stability are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Nanoscale trenches at a material interface can reduce effective thermal boundary resistance (TBReff) by increasing contact area.
The TBReff reduction mechanism is applicable to interfaces involving refractory high-entropy alloys and plasma-facing materials.
Nanopatterning does not degrade the bulk mechanical strength or irradiation resistance of the HEA.
The nanopatterns remain dimensionally stable and intact under thermal cycling up to 1000 °C and irradiation.
